title: Aside vs Claude in Chrome: Keep Claude, Change the Browser
summary: Aside vs Claude in Chrome compared: keep your Claude Pro or Max plan and use it in Aside. Setup, model choice, memory, passwords, autofill and signups.
body_markdown:
On November 2, a game developer used Claude Code with Claude in Chrome to read their earlier Reddit post and draft an update.[Claude could write the update in chat but couldn’t open the original post](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/95326#issuecomment-6592726787) . In June,[another Claude Code user reported](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/65931) that the extension couldn’t read Instagram even after they approved the site. Neither report establishes a blanket ban on social media.


You can keep Claude and change the browser it works in. Connect your Claude Pro or Max plan to Aside and ask it to collect comments with links back to the originals. Our team used Aside for read-only Reddit research in November. On Instagram,[our walkthrough](https://aside.com/blog/free-manychat-alternative-instagram-comment-link) shows a scheduled task answering five comments requesting a link.


Aside and Claude in Chrome compared across setup, models, memory, passwords, autofill, and signups.


## What does the Claude Chrome extension do?#


[Claude in Chrome](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12012173) is Anthropic’s extension for paid Claude plans. It can read pages you’re signed in to, click, type, fill forms and work across tabs while Chrome stays open. The same extension has two side-panel experiences: classic and Cowork.


Anthropic says the Cowork side panel runs on Max, Ultra and Team plans, on Pro as the rollout reaches each account, and on Enterprise where an admin has enabled it. In that version, conversations are saved to your history, and your skills, plugins and connectors work in the panel. The classic extension has saved shortcuts that you can schedule.


Anthropic also documents local file work through Claude Desktop and browser tools for Claude Code. The comparison is about where your work lives and which models can use it, not whether Claude can act on websites.


## Browser setup: Claude Chrome extension or Aside?#


Claude in Chrome adds an agent to a browser you already use. Aside is a separate browser with the agent built in. That changes the setup: install an extension in Chrome, or move your browsing into Aside and connect a model provider, including your existing Claude subscription.


Signing in connects model access; it is not a migration of your Claude chats, projects or connector setup. Aside supplies its own task instructions, memory and tools. Using Claude in Aside is not the same product experience as using Claude in Chrome, even when the model is the same.


In Aside, each[task](https://docs.aside.com/help/tasks) has its own model and working-folder controls. Keep the source links and notes from one research task in a project folder, then use them in the next task without changing browsers.


If you mainly want Claude in your existing Chrome tabs, the extension is the simpler setup. Claude also has a[built-in browser in Desktop](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/16607400) and a[Claude Code integration](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/chrome) . Choose Aside if you want to keep the same browser workspace when you change models.


## Model choice: which providers can you use in Aside?#


Aside is model-agnostic: you can choose among supported model providers for each task, rather than commit every browser task to one AI vendor. Claude can remain your default. You can also connect another supported subscription, use your own API key or run a compatible local model. Claude in Chrome uses Claude models.


In[Settings > Models](https://docs.aside.com/help/ai) , you can choose from four kinds of provider:


- Models included with your Aside plan.
- A supported subscription, such as Claude Pro or Max, ChatGPT with Codex access, GitHub Copilot or Grok.
- An API key, for example from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI or OpenRouter.
- A local model through Ollama or LM Studio, if the model supports tool calling.


You can also change the model inside a task. The task keeps its message history. If the new model has a smaller context window, Aside may summarize earlier messages to fit.


The limits are worth stating plainly:


- Check the provider list in Settings for the models available to your account.
- Model-agnostic does not mean identical capability. Models differ in supported inputs, context limits and how well they use tools. Local models also depend on your computer’s resources.
- Your own subscription or API key still carries its provider's rate limits or costs.


## Memory: where does your context live?#


Aside saves[memory](https://aside.com/features/memory) as Markdown files on your computer, under your Aside account and not under any one model provider. You can open them, change a line or delete a file. History lookup is separate and searches pages you have visited. Context awareness, which captures your activity, is opt-in and off by default.


An illustration, not a tested run: you ask Claude for a weekly pricing report and save the required format in Aside’s memory. Later you choose an OpenAI model. Aside can supply the same saved format and project context, without rebuilding that setup in another app. You still need to check the new model’s output.


History lookup lets you ask, “Which pricing page did I open last week?” It does not depend on enabling Context Awareness. That gives the task another source of context beyond what you have written in a chat.


Claude has editable memory too. Anthropic’s[chat and cloud Cowork memory](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11817273-use-claude-s-chat-search-and-memory-to-build-on-previous-context) is shared through your Claude account, with separate project memory.[Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory) also supports local instruction and memory files. Aside’s difference is a browser workspace whose saved context can be reused across the model providers you connect, not the existence of memory or local files alone.


In Aside’s[standard multi-device setup](https://docs.aside.com/help/devices) , memory, chats and projects stay on the computer where you created them. Claude’s cloud Cowork sessions can be reopened on other devices. Switching models within one Aside installation is different from syncing that workspace across computers.


One limit to be clear about: local storage describes where the files live. When you use a cloud model such as Claude, relevant memory can be included in prompts sent to that provider.


## Passwords: how does Aside Vault differ?#


Aside includes its own password manager,[Aside Vault](https://docs.aside.com/help/password-manager) . It saves logins and autofills them for the agent without returning the raw password through that autofill flow. You do not need a separate 1Password account to use it, and it supports macOS and Windows.


When a task reaches a login page, Aside checks the site URL and your access policy before using a matching saved login. For a CRM task, that means using the saved credential rather than pasting it into the conversation. The website still receives the credential through the form.


You can unlock Vault with Touch ID or Windows Hello. In[password settings](https://docs.aside.com/help/passwords) , choose Always allow, While unlocked or Never for agent access; the documented default is Always allow. Imported items can override that policy individually. You can also exclude domains from autofill. Review those settings before using a sensitive account.


Claude can use saved passwords too. Anthropic’s current[1Password for Claude](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15936181) beta requires Claude Desktop on macOS, Claude in Chrome and a 1Password account. You approve credential use per task with biometrics, and 1Password keeps passwords and one-time codes out of Claude’s context. Aside’s distinction is a built-in, cross-platform vault, not a claim that Claude cannot sign in or that Aside is inherently safer.


Some sites still require a human step for identity checks, MFA or passkey approval. A password manager does not remove every login interruption.


## Autofill: can you use saved cards and identities?#


Aside Vault supports saved payment-card and identity items, not just website logins. Its autofill tools can place those details into supported forms without returning their field values through the tool. Anthropic’s[1Password integration for Claude](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/15936181) explicitly supports logins and one-time codes, but not card or identity items.


For cards, Aside’s supported fields include the cardholder name, number, expiration and CVV. Identity items cover details such as a name, email, phone number and address. The agent selects the saved item; access still depends on your Vault settings and whether the form is supported.


A practical use is preparing a checkout form or filling contact details, then stopping for review. Autofilling a card is not the same as submitting a payment, and filling identity details is not identity verification. The destination page receives the values, so use a site you trust.


This compares the credential integrations, not every way Claude could type information into a form. It also does not guarantee that filled values can never appear in later page content or screenshots.


## Signups: can the agent create a new password?#


Aside can generate a password, fill it into a signup form and save the resulting login in Vault without returning the generated password through the tool. Anthropic’s[Chrome permissions guide](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12902446) lists account creation as prohibited. That is a difference between the products’ workflows, not between the underlying models’ intelligence.


The password workflow has three parts. Vault generates a password using the site’s requirements. The agent receives a reference to that password, not its characters, and can use it in the password and confirmation fields. After signup succeeds, the credential can be saved for the next login.


For example, when you ask Aside to set up a new software account, it can handle the password-generation and storage steps as part of the task. That does not promise every signup will complete: email verification, passkey approval, identity checks or other site requirements can still need you.


Review the account details, terms and any trial or payment commitment before submission. Password generation is not permission to create an account you did not ask for.


## What are users saying?#


Users reported access problems on Reddit and Instagram, but others used Claude in Chrome on LinkedIn. Here’s what happened on each site, alongside Aside user reports and our own tests. These were separate runs, not a head-to-head test.


Task Claude in Chrome Aside


Research Reddit discussions A[game developer](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/95326#issuecomment-6592726787) reported that on Nov 2, Claude in Chrome couldn’t open their own earlier Reddit post to draft an update.[Another user](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/95326#issuecomment-6066903108) said support called the access problem a bug, not a policy. In our November research, Aside collected Reddit comments and links, including[a reader listing Aside among several Arc alternatives](https://www.reddit.com/r/ArcBrowser/comments/1l0qf8c/comment/19s8zfjulqrlu/) . We didn’t post or reply.


Respond to Instagram comments In June,[a Claude Code user](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/65931) reported that the Chrome extension couldn’t open or read Instagram after they approved the site. They never reached the comments. Our[Instagram walkthrough](https://aside.com/blog/free-manychat-alternative-instagram-comment-link) shows a scheduled task checking a signed-in post and answering five comments that requested a link.


Review LinkedIn posts[Christopher Alarcon](https://christopheralarcon.com/blog/claude-in-chrome) used Claude in Chrome to read his signed-in LinkedIn analytics, identify posts with the most impressions and suggest new hooks. LinkedIn worked in his test. In our November 16 test, Aside saved five company-page posts to a CSV with dates, reactions, comment counts and links. The next section shows the task and result.


Write to Google Sheets In the September 2025 preview,[PCMag’s Ruben Circelli](https://www.pcmag.com/articles/claudes-ai-chrome-extension-wont-revolutionize-web-browsing-yet-but-i-like) asked for a Warframe tracker. Claude opened a sheet but didn’t fill it in. An[Aside user on GPTers](https://www.gpters.org/nocode/post/review-95-printers-automating-AVLeCOgHUszGLXN) checked 107 saved toner entries in Sheets: 67 direct readings and 40 estimates from gauge bars. Seven failed lookups were skipped, preserving earlier values.


Find products on Coupang[Habni](https://have-been.com/en/posts/aside-browser) was already signed in, but Claude showed a site safety restriction in August 2026. A[September 2026 walkthrough (0:35)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9ZzF5iGj0BM&t=35s) shows Aside searching the same retailer and opening cordless vacuum listings.


Shop on Amazon[Christopher Alarcon](https://christopheralarcon.com/blog/claude-in-chrome) had Claude fill his grocery cart and explicitly told it to stop before checkout.[Anthropic’s guide](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/12902446) lists purchases as prohibited.[G2 reviewer Roman S.](https://www.g2.com/products/aside/reviews/aside-review-14011460) wrote, “I can easily place orders on Amazon with Aside.” He didn’t say who completed checkout.


## What does a completed Aside task look like?#


On November 16, we asked Aside to collect the five most recent posts from our LinkedIn page and save them as a CSV without interacting with the posts. It returned a table in chat and a file we could open.


The exact prompt:


> On LinkedIn, open the Aside page (linkedin.com/showcase/asidehq) and collect its 5 most recent posts: date, the first 80 characters, reactions and comments. Save them as aside-linkedin-posts.csv and show me the table. Read only: don’t react, comment, follow or message anyone, and keep it to three page loads or fewer.


The November 16 Aside task, showing the original prompt and the first three result rows.


The CSV has five rows: three original posts and two reposts. Each row has the date, the first 80 characters, the reaction and comment counts, and a direct link to the post. We opened the file to confirm it matches the table.


“Don’t react, comment, follow or message anyone” was part of the prompt, not a technical lock on the account.


We didn’t record which model ran this task or run the same prompt in Claude in Chrome. The CSV is evidence of the result, not a speed or model comparison.


## Claude Computer Use vs. Aside Computer Use#


Claude has its own[computer-use feature](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14128542-let-claude-use-your-computer-in-cowork) in Claude Desktop, separate from the Chrome extension. With your permission, it can open apps, click and type on macOS or Windows. It’s in beta for Pro, Max and Ultra users in Cowork and Claude Code.


[Aside Computer Use ranked #1 on macOS in Cua Driver Bench](https://aside.com/blog/aside-computer-use-ranks-number-one-in-cua-driver-bench) . With Claude Opus 5.5, it passed 88 of 90 trials (97.8%). Scale tested desktop-control tools, not Claude Cowork or the Chrome extension.


Claude Computer Use Aside Computer Use


In[Claude Cowork](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/14128542-let-claude-use-your-computer-in-cowork) , Claude tries a connector or browser first. If the task needs a desktop app, it asks permission to open it, then clicks and types. On macOS 15 or later, it works in background windows by default. You can keep Claude as your model and let Aside control the desktop apps. In Scale’s Mac test, Claude Opus 5.5 using Aside finished 50 of 50 foreground runs and 38 of 40 background runs without interrupting a simulated user typing in another window.


The[versioned benchmark results](https://huggingface.co/datasets/earakely-scale/CuaDriverBench-AgentEnv/blob/ca3d569ef93c1987f75bf00663e3114c0ed601ac/README.md) show why the tool matters even with the model held constant: Opus 5.5 passed 88 of 90 trials with Aside and 62 of 90 with Cua Driver v0.47.10. Cua Driver is a separate tool, not Anthropic’s computer-use feature.


## The best of both worlds: use Claude Models with Aside Browser#


If Claude is the model you want, keep it. Connect your Claude Pro or Max plan to Aside and use Claude to work across your signed-in tabs and save results to your project folder. If you switch models later, your project files and instructions stay in Aside.


Choose Claude to use a Pro or Max subscription you already pay for.


**Connect your Claude subscription**


1. [Install Aside](https://aside.com/download) . During setup, choose Claude on the AI subscription screen.
2. Already set up Aside? Open[Settings > Models > Providers](https://docs.aside.com/help/ai) , select Connect, then Claude Subscription.
3. Sign in with Anthropic and approve the connection. You don’t need an API key.
4. Start a task and choose Claude in the model picker.


In Settings > Models, look for “Subscription” under Claude to confirm you connected your plan rather than an API key.


Changing the task model can also update the default for future tasks. Check the selected model before starting.


Claude Subscription and an Anthropic API key are separate entries in Aside. If you use a key, requests use your Claude Console organization’s billing and any applicable API credits. Check which provider you selected before a long run.


Try a read-only task on a post you own:


> Open my latest LinkedIn post. Summarize the questions people asked in the visible comments, and save a note with the post link and a draft answer for each question. If you can’t read the comments, tell me. Don’t post, react or send any messages.


Check the note against the comments before you use any of the drafts.


## What does Aside cost if you already pay for Claude?#


[Aside Free](https://aside.com/pricing) includes 500 monthly credits and up to three active routines. On monthly billing, Aside Pro is $20 and Aside Max is $200. Those are Aside prices, separate from your Claude subscription. You don’t need a paid Aside plan just to connect a supported provider.


### Questions Claude users ask#


**Can I use my Claude subscription in Aside?**


Yes. You can use Claude in Aside by connecting your Claude Pro or Max account.


**Can I bring my existing passwords into Aside?**


Yes. Open Settings > Passwords > Import, choose the source and follow its import flow. Aside supports source-specific exports and a generic CSV format. Review the imported items and their agent-access settings before using them. See the[password import guide](https://docs.aside.com/help/passwords) .


**Does Aside work on Windows?**


Yes. Aside runs on macOS 15 or later, Windows 10 version 22H2 and Windows 11.


**Do routines run while my computer is asleep?**


For[local Aside routines](https://docs.aside.com/help/automation) , keep your computer awake and Aside open.[Claude’s cloud Cowork schedules](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/13854387) can run against connected services while your computer sleeps. Tasks that use your own Chrome browser need your computer awake, with Chrome and Claude Desktop open.
